result.description:
Ready to stop reporting on the business and start influencing it?

Some finance roles are all about producing reports. This isn't one of them.

At MiHaven, we're looking for a Financial Controller who wants a seat at the table. Someone who sees beyond the numbers, challenges the status quo and isn't afraid to ask, "There has to be a better way."

You'll work directly with our Directors, lead a small finance team and become the commercial voice behind some of our biggest business decisions.

If you're looking for a role where you can genuinely influence the future of a growing business, not just report on it,you've just found it!

The Opportunity

It's not your typical Financial Controller position. Yes, you'll oversee the finance function. Yes, you'll manage budgets, forecasts, cash flow and reporting.

But you'll also be responsible for helping shape the financial success of major construction projects, providing the commercial insight that keeps projects on track and ensuring every dollar works harder for the business.

We're looking for someone who's curious. Someone who challenges. Someone who sees opportunities where others see spreadsheets. You can check out the day to day via the PD which is located on our careers page.

About You

You might already be a Financial Controller. Or perhaps you're the Finance Manager who's already doing the work but hasn't been given the title. Either way, you'll bring:

    Strong commercial acumen
    Exceptional financial reporting and forecasting skills
    Confidence leading people and holding your team accountable
    The ability to influence operational leaders
    A proactive mindset focused on improving systems and processes
    The confidence to speak up, challenge ideas and contribute strategically

Construction experience would be great,but it's not essential.

Commercial thinking is.
Why you'll love this role

This is one of those rare opportunities where your contribution won't disappear into layers of management.

Your work will be seen.

Your ideas will be heard.

Your decisions will make a difference.

You'll enjoy:

    Negotiable salary based on experience
    Option to include company vehicle and/or fuel card as part of remuneration package
    On-site parking
    Full-time office-based role in Cairns
    Genuine autonomy
    Direct access to the Directors
    The opportunity to build something better

If you're ready to step into a role where you'll influence decisions not just report on them, we'd love to hear from you.

For a confidential discussion, connect with our Recruitment Business Partner Victoria Williams on 03 9691 4712.

To apply for this job go to: https://mihavenjobs.recruitmenthub.com.au/Jobs

Applications close 06 August 2026

result.description: MILANOE CONSTRUCTIONS PTY LTD   Company:  MILANOE CONSTRUCTIONS PTY LTD trading as De Walkers Group   Position:  Quantity Surveyor   Job Type:  Full-Time, Permanent   Salary:  AUD $80,000 – $87,000 per annum plus superannuation   Location:  Scoresby and Clyde, VIC   About us   MILANOE CONSTRUCTIONS PTY LTD, trading as De Walkers Group, is a Victorian residential construction and project management business specialising in custom-built homes and multi-unit residential developments.  De Walkers Group was established to address a need in the Victorian residential construction market for a builder that places clients at the centre of the construction process. Our approach is founded on transparent communication, proactive client involvement and a strong commitment to quality throughout every stage of a project, from the initial consultation through to final handover.  Our custom-build projects include architecturally designed residences tailored to each client’s land, lifestyle and long-term vision. We also provide end-to-end design and construction services for townhouses, dual occupancies and residential apartment developments, managing projects from the approval stage through to completion and handover.  We undertake residential construction projects across Inner Melbourne, Bayside, Melbourne’s eastern and south-eastern suburbs, the Gippsland region, the Mornington Peninsula and the Yarra Ranges.  Due to our continued business growth and expanding portfolio of residential construction projects, we are seeking a qualified and experienced Quantity Surveyor to join our team on a full-time permanent basis.  This is an excellent opportunity for a reliable and detail-oriented professional to become an integral member of De Walkers Group and contribute to the cost planning, procurement and successful delivery of our residential construction projects.      Responsibilities   As a Quantity Surveyor, your primary responsibilities will include:   Obtaining quotations from subcontractors, suppliers and vendors, collating and assessing the quotations received, and providing recommendations to management.  Reviewing architectural drawings, engineering plans, project specifications and contract documentation to determine the labour, materials, equipment and other resources required for each project.  Preparing detailed construction cost estimates based on project drawings, specifications and supporting contract documentation.  Undertaking accurate quantity take-offs using modern estimating technologies and recognised methods of measurement.  Preparing bills of quantities, schedules of rates, tender documentation and other project costing documents.  Maintaining and regularly updating project cost data to reflect current construction material, labour, subcontractor and market rates.  Preparing rate analyses and cost comparisons to assist management with tender evaluation and procurement decisions.  Assisting with the preparation and evaluation of tenders, subcontractor packages and supplier procurement documentation.  Monitoring project expenditure throughout all stages of construction to ensure that projects remain aligned with the approved baseline cost plan and budget.  Identifying cost deviations, potential overruns and financial risks and recommending appropriate corrective measures.  Preparing regular project cost reports, cash-flow forecasts, cost-to-complete assessments and financial updates for management.  Identifying and establishing the scope of proposed changes to construction works.  Evaluating and pricing client change requests, contract variations and extension of time claims.  Undertaking rate analysis and participating in negotiations relating to variations, additional works and contractual claims.  Reviewing, evaluating and certifying subcontractor and contractor interim progress claims and final payment applications.  Conducting site inspections and taking site measurements in conjunction with relevant trades to verify work completed and quantities claimed.  Assessing the value of completed works and reconciling actual project expenditure against the approved construction budget.  Updating project programmes and construction schedules to reflect the actual progress of works across active projects.  Monitoring project milestones and assisting the project team to identify delays or issues that may affect project costs or completion dates.  Coordinating with directors, project managers, site supervisors, subcontractors, consultants, suppliers, clients and other project stakeholders.  Assisting with contract administration and maintaining accurate records relating to project costs, procurement, variations, claims and payments.  Supporting the delivery of projects within the approved budget, agreed timeframes, contractual requirements and applicable construction standards.    Qualifications and Experience   Applicants must possess:   A relevant qualification in Quantity Surveying or a closely related construction discipline.  A minimum of three years’ relevant work experience as a Quantity Surveyor.  Demonstrated experience in residential construction cost estimating, quantity take-offs, tendering, procurement and cost control.  Experience preparing bills of quantities, cost plans, tender documentation, progress claim assessments and variation evaluations.  Sound knowledge of residential construction processes, materials, subcontractor trades and construction cost management principles.  Experience interpreting architectural drawings, engineering plans, specifications and contract documentation.  Strong numerical, analytical and technical problem-solving skills.  Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.  Strong organisational and time-management skills.  The ability to manage competing priorities and work across multiple construction projects.  Strong written and verbal communication skills.  The ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a project t...  Read more: https://workinitiatives.com.au/job/details?id=6081788

Position: Restaurant Manager
Position Type: Full Time
Salary: $75,000 - $85,000 p.a plus Super
Employer Name: The Savoury Dining Penrith Pty Ltd
A.B.N. 23 641 017 674
Job Location: 407-411 High St, Penrith, NSW, 2750,  AUSTRALIA
Advertising Period: 7 days - 22 Jul 2026 > 29 Jul 2026

Please include Reference: J1705-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Summary

Savoury Dining Penrith is a vibrant Southeast Asian restaurant bringing the flavours of street food to Western Sydney through an All You Can Eat dining experience. The restaurant celebrates dishes such as pho, banh xeo, laksa, Pad Thai and green curry, refined by dedicated chefs to create a generous and memorable dining experience. Designed for families, groups and food lovers, Savoury Dining offers buffet dining, à la carte, takeaway, function and catering options. With authentic flavours, friendly service and a relaxed atmosphere, it gives locals an easy way to explore the best of Southeast Asia in one place.

Website: www.thesavourydining.com.au 

About The Position
The Savoury Dining Penrith Pty Ltd is looking for a Restaurant Manager with a minimum of 3 years of relevant experience and a relevant diploma.  This role reports to the Director.

The typical job responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:

- Welcome and assist patrons upon arrival, provide them with menus, and take their food and beverage orders. 
- Facilitate easy reservation processes by phone or in person.
- Collaborate with the head chef on planning menus. Identify emerging trends and opportunities, innovate new dishes, and ensure accurate pricing on menus to optimise profitability. 
- Monitor inventory levels, place orders for ingredients, beverages, and supplies, and maintain adequate stock to meet customer demand. 
- Review invoices and track expenses for efficient financial management.
- Maintain consistency in service standards by implementing standard operating procedures and conducting regular training and quality checks. 
- Organise and oversee functions and events such as private parties and corporate gatherings.
- Handle financial transactions, including managing the cash register, processing payments, and reconciling daily transactions.
- Ensure cleanliness and safety standards are upheld, adhering to health and safety regulations. Develop cleaning schedules and address maintenance issues promptly.
- Collaborate with corporate clients to tailor menus for events and coordinate with staff to ensure seamless execution.
- Focus on achieving high levels of customer satisfaction and retention. 
- Implement roster structures to optimise labour costs.
- Recruit, train, and supervise front and back-of-house managers and supervisors, including performance evaluations and ongoing support.
- Develop and implement business strategies to achieve sales targets, monitor financial performance, control costs, and maximise overall profitability of the restaurant.

Applicants must meet the following minimum requirements to be considered for the role:

- A relevant diploma.
- A minimum of 3 years of relevant experience.
- Demonstrated genuine passion for the hospitality sector and restaurant management.
- Strong verbal communication skills, enabling effective liaison with staff, customers, and suppliers.
- Excellent organisational abilities to oversee key restaurant operations, including staff scheduling, inventory control, and financial budgeting.
- Outstanding interpersonal and leadership skills, with the ability to motivate and inspire team members while maintaining a positive and collaborative work environment.
- Superior time management skills to ensure efficient daily operations and consistent, timely service delivery.
- Proven multitasking capabilities to successfully manage multiple responsibilities at once, including team supervision, customer service, and administrative tasks.
- Proactive attitude toward adopting new technologies, emerging industry trends, and modern management practices to enhance operational efficiency and customer satisfaction.
- Strong capability to effectively oversee all areas of restaurant operations, including front-of-house, back-of-house, and administrative functions.

Please include Reference: J1705-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Due to the volume of applicants, only those meeting the minimum standards will be considered and only successful applicants will be contacted.  Thank you for your interest in the role.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Associate Midwifery Unit Manager 

Full time or Part Time 

Malvern 

We're building for the better!

By 2036, more than 150,000 patients will look to us for healthcare every year.

At Cabrini Health we champion community, compassion and career fulfilment. Our teams are united by the shared purpose of making a meaningful contribution to exceptional, patient-centred care in well- resourced, world class facilities that inspire you to perform at your best and continuously grow professionally.

About the Role:

Our Maternity department is supported by a multidisciplinary team, including midwives, registered nurses, and lactation consultants, working together across 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. 

As the Associate Midwifery Unit Manager (AMUM) at Cabrini, you will collaborate closely with the Maternity Services Manager and the clinical management team to provide strong, effective leadership. Your role will involve promoting excellence in clinical practice and supporting the strategic direction of the Maternity department. 

Key Responsibilities:

Provide leadership and operational direction. 

Coordinate and oversee the delivery of patient care, ensuring it aligns with Cabrini's standards and values. 

Implement and monitor hospital policies, procedures, and protocols. 

Hold accountability for the ward in the absence of the Maternity Services Manager. 

Foster a collaborative and supportive environment for staff development and patient care.

About You:

We are seeking a passionate and dedicated Registered Midwife with: 

At least two years of experience in a leadership or similar role.

Demonstrated clinical and leadership skills. 

Current AHPRA registration as a Registered Midwife.

A current Working with Children Check. 

Commitment to quality patient care and outcomes. 

Ability to work within the Mission and Values of the organisation. 

Flexibility and a positive attitude. 

Attention to detail

What we offer:

Salary packaging: up to $15,900 tax-free each year, plus $2650 meal & entertainment card benefits

Convenience: Vibrant Malvern location, close to local shops, cafes and public transport

Travel Perks: Myki Commuter discounted fares

A commitment to health and well-being initiatives including discounted access to a wide range of gyms, pools, and fitness facilities through Fitness Passport

Access to a range of retail offers, discounted hospital services and savings on eligible private health fund services

If you're a passionate midwifery leader looking to step into a rewarding and influential role within a supportive team, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now and be part of shaping the future of maternity care at Cabrini.

To view the full position description, please click here.

Enquiries should be directed to: Sarah Wealands - Maternity Services Manager - 03 9508 1664

Apply early! This role may close sooner than the listed closing date if we find the right candidate - so don't wait to get your application in.

Does this sound like your new role? Bring your skills and enthusiasm to Cabrini Health and help optimise the patient experience and health outcomes for our community.

Cabrini Health acknowledges the importance of creating a work environment that is welcoming, safe, equitable and inclusive for people of all backgrounds and abilities. Inclusion is core to our mission.

As part of our commitment to Reconciliation and Closing the Gap in employment related outcomes, we encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples.

Working for Cabrini

Cabrini Health is a Catholic, private, for-purpose health service located in Melbourne's southeast. Inspired by the mission and ethic of care of the Cabrini Sisters, providing quality, compassionate care to our community for more than 75 years.

There is something special about Cabrini Health. Our highly skilled staff and specialists incorporate clinical research, innovative models of care and state-of-the-art technology to deliver the best possible care and outcomes for our patients. We demonstrate our mission to serve our community through outreach programs that support asylum seekers, provide healthcare in rural communities and in underdeveloped countries.

Our size, reputation and growth strategy ensure genuine opportunities for our people to learn, grow and realise potential.

Our values: Compassion - Integrity - Courage - Respect

MANDATORY FOR ALL NEW STAFF TO CABRINI

Employment with Cabrini Health will be based on satisfactory background checks such as professional references, National Police Check, vaccinations for annual Influenza plus a Working with Children Check (WWCC) may also be requested. Vaccination for COVID-19 is highly recommended.    Click here to Apply now →

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Temporary Full Time until 26 March 2027
Position Classification: Nurse Mgr Gde 4
Remuneration: 167023.6 - 169961.26 full-time equivalent base salary range (+12% super + 17.5% leave loading and salary packaging) 
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: REQ679770
Located in: Westmead
Applications Close: Midnight on 31 July 2026
For role related queries or questions contact Michael Sharp on Michael.Sharp1@health.nsw.gov.au
 

At the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, every role helps children and young people live their healthiest lives.

As the largest paediatric health service in Australia, we care for thousands of children each year, in hospital and at home. Our people are united by compassion, collaboration and excellence in care.

An exciting temporary 6-month opportunity is available for an experienced nursing leader with a passion for innovation, quality and patient safety. As the Nurse Manager Level 4 - Clinical Products Manager, you will lead the strategic management of clinical products across the health service, ensuring clinicians have access to safe, effective and evidence-based products that support exceptional patient care. Working collaboratively with clinicians, procurement teams and key stakeholders, you will drive product evaluation, standardisation, innovation and value-based healthcare initiatives that improve patient outcomes and organisational performance. 

If you're a collaborative leader who enjoys influencing change and making a lasting impact across healthcare, we'd love to hear from you.

What you'll be doing
 

The Nurse Manager will lead and manage the delivery of nursing services and service improvements within their 
portfolio within a culture that promotes the CORE values of NSW Health: Collaboration, Openness, Respect and 
Empowerment. 

The Nurse Manager will develop an operational plan for the nursing service, identify and actively seek to develop a 
staffing profile reflective of the service needs and develop and manage a nursing budget within the portfolio. 

The Nurse Manager will develop the potential of staff, identify develop and facilitate a range of strategies to ensure 
nursing staff have the knowledge and skills required to undertake their roles. 

The Nurse Manager will undertake planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of performance within the 
portfolio for individual staff and the team. 

The Nurse Manager will utilise a range of communication strategies to foster shared decision making, responsibility 
and accountability. 
 

Additional Benefits (where applicable): Flexible work opportunities, Salary packaging and meal entertainment benefits, accrued days off (ADOs), fitness passport, employee assistance program (EAP)

How to Apply:
Click 'Apply Online' and submit your application including:

A resume (maximum 5 pages) outlining your experience 

Responses to the questions below:

Current authority to practice as a Registered Nurse with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA)

Relevant postgraduate tertiary qualifications and nursing leadership and management experience

Demonstrated ability to develop, direct and lead a team to achieve organisational objectives

Demonstrated ability to function effectively as part of a senior management team and to collaborate with other health professionals and disciplines in the management of health care services

Demonstrated ability to manage conflicting priorities and meet deadlines in an environment of high volume-pressure

Demonstrated high level communication and negotiation skills

Demonstrated experience in change management, negotiating competing interests and conflict resolution

Demonstrated ability to manage resources effectively within designated timeframes and budgets

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Child Safe Standards:
SCHN is committed to maintaining a child-safe environment that respects and upholds the rights of children and young people, in line with NSW Health's commitment to the Child Safe Standards. We aim to ensure that children and young people feel safe, supported, and included in their care. All current and prospective staff are expected to prioritise the safety, welfare, and well-being of children and young people, actively working to protect them from harm and abuse.

Additional Information: 

SCHN is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values diversity, recognising that a diverse workforce strengthens our culture and enhances the care we provide to children, young people and their families.

Permanent NSW Health roles require Australian citizenship or permanent residency. Temporary visa holders may be considered where no suitable Australian citizen or permanent resident is identified.

NSW Health vaccination and screening requirements must be met prior to commencement. 

This position requires a Working with Children Check (WWCC) issued by the Office of the Children's Guardian.

Where required, overseas qualifications must be formally assessed by the Department of Education or relevant authority for recognition in Australia.

An Eligibility List may be created for future temporary full or part time vacancies.
